name: Type IV Composite Gas Cylinders: Hydrogen, CNG Cascades & Lightweight Storage
scope: Indian listed exposure to carbon-fibre-wrapped, polymer-lined Type IV cylinders for CNG cascades, LPG, and hydrogen mobility: certification, orders, capacity, inputs, valuation and catalysts.

summary.one_line: In India, Type IV cylinders earn real money only from CNG cascades and LPG, and only at Time Technoplast (about Rs 763 cr of composite sales in FY26, ~12.5% of group revenue). Hydrogen is still at the approval and pilot stage. Confidence Petroleum's Nagpur Type 4 plant and EKC's US Type 4 capex have no disclosed revenue yet.
key_points: Type IV composite cylinders weigh about 15-20 kg, against about 60-70 kg for conventional steel CNG cylinders. Indian designs are reported to burst above 600 bar, against a 400 bar regulatory requirement. Carbon fibre is not made in India and has to be imported (S9).

Global forecasts disagree. GMI sizes composite Type IV/V hydrogen tanks at USD 1.4 bn in 2026, rising to USD 7.7 bn by 2035 (20.9% CAGR) (S10). HTF projects 14.7% CAGR for 2026-2034 on a different definition (S11).

Time Technoplast is the only listed Indian maker with certified Type IV products and firm orders. Its FY26 composite revenue was about Rs 763 cr: Rs 482 cr from CNG cascades, Rs 236 cr from LPG cylinders and Rs 45 cr from other composites, roughly 12.5% of Rs 6,105 cr consolidated sales (S4).
In 2026 Time Technoplast disclosed two PSU orders for Type IV CNG cascades: Rs 115.56 cr on 17 March and Rs 87.53 cr on 31 August. Each is to be executed within one year (S2, S3).

Hydrogen is still at the approval stage. PESO cleared a 150 L Type IV hydrogen cylinder in June 2024 and Bureau Veritas followed in May 2025 (S6). The April 2026 PESO design approval for a 250 L cylinder still required prototype joint inspection and testing, with validation expected within about 90 days (S1). No hydrogen revenue has been disclosed.

Confidence Petroleum markets 200/250/350 bar Type 4 cylinders through its subsidiary Silversky Exim. Its June 2026 presentation still called the Butibori, Nagpur plant 'upcoming' and gave no capex, capacity or commissioning date (S15, S17). Its FY26 accounts carried a modified audit opinion over GST input-tax-credit reconciliation (S16).
Everest Kanto's board approved USD 5.5 mn of capex at its US subsidiary for larger-diameter and Type 4 cylinders (S18). Meanwhile its Q1 FY27 revenue fell 10.5% YoY and PAT fell 41.5% (S19).

The market has not priced in a theme. Time Technoplast trades at Rs 157, near its Rs 154 low (high Rs 220) (S12). EKC is down 35% over one year (S14). Confidence (Rs 69.6) is about 2.6x its Rs 27 low, but the rise came alongside a step-up in its LPG business, not anything Type 4 (S13).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Time Technoplast is the only listed name already earning revenue from Type IV CNG cascades and LPG cylinders. Management guides 25-30% volume CAGR for composites (S4), and it has 2026 PSU cascade orders of about Rs 203 cr (S2, S3).
City gas distributors and OMCs buying cascades and lightweight LPG cylinders (e.g. HPCL's 10 kg 'HP Navya' composite cylinder pilot with Swiggy Instamart) gain logistics and safety benefits (S5).
Reliance is building composites for hydrogen storage and a carbon-fibre facility at Hazira (S22). That is the only identified route to localising the main imported input (S9).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Hydrogen volumes are pilot-scale: 70 vehicles and 16 refuelling stations across 12 NGHM pilots, with only Rs 41.58 cr of the Rs 410.77 cr earmarked actually released (S20).

New domestic competition: NTF Energy Solutions (unlisted, TDB loan support) is targeting September 2027 market entry with Type IV CNG cylinders. It is starting with passenger vehicles and plans to move into cascades later (S8, S9).
Confidence Petroleum has a qualified FY26 audit (S16), Rs 761 cr of borrowings and 9% ROCE (S13), and no disclosed Type 4 output (S15).
Steel-cylinder makers such as EKC face weaker CNG volumes (Q1 FY27 revenue -10.5% YoY) (S19), while their own Type 4 effort sits outside India (S18).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Completion of PESO prototype validation for Time Technoplast's 250 L hydrogen cylinder (S1), and the first hydrogen supply order.
Further PSU/CGD Type IV cascade tenders. The Mar-2026 and Aug-2026 orders are due for execution by about Mar-2027 and Aug-2027 (S2, S3).
Any filing by Confidence Petroleum giving commissioning, certification or revenue from the Silversky Butibori Type 4 plant (S15).
Commissioning of NGHM pilots (2025 round targeted within 18-24 months) (S21), and Reliance's Hazira carbon-fibre timeline (S22).

sections.title: What Type IV cylinders are and where demand comes from

blocks.text: Type IV cylinders pair a non-metallic polymer liner with a full overwrap of carbon (or glass) fibre composite. Type I cylinders are all-metal (steel), and Types II-III use metal liners with partial or full composite wraps. Time Technoplast describes its product as a thermoplastic liner wrapped in carbon or glass fibre, lighter than steel or aluminium cylinders (S2). The TDB-backed NTF design uses a corrosion-free polymer liner with an optimised CFRP layup and burst pressure above 600 bar (S8). Each cylinder weighs about 15-20 kg, against about 60-70 kg for conventional steel CNG cylinders (S9).

blocks.text: Market-research estimates vary with definition. Global Market Insights (Sept-2026) sizes composite Type IV and V hydrogen tanks at USD 1.1 bn in 2025 and USD 1.4 bn in 2026, rising to USD 7.7 bn by 2035 (20.9% CAGR). It names hydrogen mobility, infrastructure investment and lightweighting as the drivers. Asia Pacific is the largest region (USD 552 mn in 2025), and Hexagon Purus leads with over 11.4% share (S10). HTF Market Intelligence forecasts a 14.7% CAGR for 2026-2034 for Type IV hydrogen vessels (S11). For India, Time Technoplast expects the CNG composite market to grow above 25% CAGR. It puts the CNG-cascade TAM at about Rs 1,500 cr, citing a MoPNG report together with its own assessment (S2).

subsections.title: Regulatory and policy drivers in India

items: PESO approvals gate market entry. Time Technoplast received a 150 L Type IV hydrogen approval in June 2024 (S6). In April 2026 it received a 250 L design approval for buses, trucks and trailers, with prototypes to be jointly inspected and validated within about 90 days (S1).

National Green Hydrogen Mission: Rs 19,744 cr outlay to FY2029-30, launched January 2023. The first round (March 2025) sanctioned 5 pilots with 37 buses/trucks and 9 refuelling stations, backed by about Rs 208 cr of central support (S21).

As of July 2026 there were 12 NGHM pilot projects covering 70 hydrogen vehicles (27 buses, 43 trucks) and 16 refuelling stations on 21 routes. Rs 410.77 cr is earmarked but only Rs 41.58 cr has been released (S20).

Technology Development Board (DST) signed a loan-support agreement with NTF Energy Solutions (unlisted, Delhi) on 7 May 2026 for a Type IV CNG cylinder plant. No amount or capacity was disclosed (S8). The cylinders are described as compatible with hydrogen-CNG blends (S9). The brief's 'NTF CNG plant for 2027' refers to this unlisted competitor, not to Time Technoplast.

blocks.text: Hydrogen blending in CNG is cited as a future government plan (S9). This edition found no notified norm or date mandating hydrogen-CNG blends, so it is not treated as a near-term volume driver.

subsections.title: Time Technoplast: the only certified, ordered Type IV maker

blocks.text: Time Technoplast's composite products sit in its Value-Added Products segment, which posted a 17.9% EBITDA margin in Q1 FY27 against 11.7% for established products (S4). By MOFSL's quarterly data, FY26 revenue was about Rs 482 cr from CNG cascades, Rs 236 cr from LPG cylinders and Rs 45 cr from other composite products. That totals about Rs 763 cr, roughly 12.5% of Rs 6,105 cr FY26 net sales (S4). Composite cylinders grew 29% YoY in Q1 FY27. Management guides 25-30% composite volume CAGR (S4). The 2026 orders (Rs 115.56 cr + Rs 87.53 cr) together equal about 42% of FY26 cascade revenue (S2, S3, S4). No hydrogen-specific revenue is disclosed.

subsections.title: Capacity builders: Confidence Petroleum and Everest Kanto

blocks.caption: Financial and governance snapshot
rows: Modified FY26 audit opinion on GST ITC (S16)

blocks.text: Confidence Petroleum announced its Type 4 entry in February 2024 through Silversky Exim, citing German technology and 200/250/350 bar ratings (S17). Its June 2026 deck still calls the Butibori plant 'upcoming' and gives no capex, capacity or date (S15). This edition could not confirm the Rs 350 cr / 1-3 lakh unit figures in the brief. FY26 consolidated EBITDA was Rs 378 cr on Rs 4,705 cr revenue (S15). The auditors' modified opinion relates to a GST input-tax-credit discrepancy, reported at Rs 1,288 lakh (S16). Everest Kanto's Type 4 effort is USD 5.5 mn of approved capex at its US subsidiary, aimed at serving the Americas (S18). It therefore reaches Indian listed earnings only through consolidation, and it is small next to Rs 1,471 cr of FY26 sales (S14).

subsections.title: Adjacent names: inputs and demand side

blocks.text: The remaining qualifying listed names are adjacent rather than cylinder makers. Reliance is localising carbon fibre and composites for hydrogen storage (S22). A Tracxn listing shows a legal entity named Reliance New Energy Carbon Fibre Cylinder Limited (S23). HPCL is the buyer of Time Technoplast's Type IV LPG cylinders (S5). GAIL and BPCL are the parents of MNGL, a past cascade customer (S7). IOCL, HPCL, BPCL, Reliance, KPIT and Ashok Leyland are NGHM hydrogen-vehicle pilot participants (S20, S21). Market-cap coverage is uneven. Pure-play exposure exists only among small caps (Time Technoplast at about Rs 7,753 cr, Confidence at about Rs 2,311 cr, EKC at about Rs 1,105 cr) (S12, S13, S14). No genuine mid-cap Type IV manufacturer was found, and the large caps are users or input suppliers for whom the theme is immaterial.

sections.title: Research house views and market pricing

blocks.text: Coverage is thin. Motilal Oswal (6 Aug 2026) is the main identified broker note on Time Technoplast. It highlights 29% YoY composite growth and 25-30% composite volume guidance. At the Rs 207 price then prevailing, it estimated P/E of 18.3x FY27E and 14.8x FY28E, and EV/EBITDA of 9.9x FY27E (S4). The stock has since fallen to Rs 157, a trailing P/E of 15.8x (S12). Market research sizes the opportunity at 14.7-20.9% CAGR depending on definition (S10, S11). This edition found no broker coverage of the Type 4 plans at Confidence Petroleum or Everest Kanto.

blocks.caption: Market pricing as of 23 Oct 2026 close
rows: ~2.6x off low; Q1 FY27 revenue more than doubled YoY (S13)

blocks.text: The rally in Confidence Petroleum lines up with its LPG-driven results: Q1 FY27 sales of Rs 2,409 cr and net profit of Rs 63 cr (S13). No Type 4 news coincides with it, so the move does not look theme-driven.

items: Slow hydrogen adoption: NGHM pilots total 70 vehicles, and only about 10% of earmarked support has been released (S20).
Certification lag: the 250 L hydrogen approval still required prototype testing as of April 2026 (S1). Bureau Veritas approval of the 150 L cylinder came about 11 months after PESO (S6).
Imported inputs: carbon fibre is not made in India (S9). Reliance's carbon-fibre plant has no disclosed commissioning date (S22). Polymer and carbon-fibre price swings are a margin risk (S5).
Competition: TDB-backed NTF Energy Solutions targets 2027 entry, with cascades planned after passenger vehicles (S8, S9). Global leaders such as Hexagon Purus hold the largest share (S10).
Lumpy order flow: cascade orders come from PSU tenders with one-year execution (S2, S3). TIME's quarterly cascade revenue fell from Rs 138 cr to Rs 104 cr QoQ in Q1 FY27 (S4).
Balance sheet and governance at Confidence Petroleum: Rs 761 cr of debt, 9% ROCE (S13) and a qualified FY26 audit (S16).

companies.name: Time Technoplast Ltd
companies.role: Makes Type IV composite CNG cascades, LPG cylinders and hydrogen cylinders. Holds PESO approvals for 150 L (S6) and 250 L (design stage) hydrogen cylinders (S1), with Bureau Veritas certification for the 150 L (S6).
companies.impact: Composites were about 12.5% of FY26 sales at segment EBITDA margins near 18% (S4). 2026 PSU orders of Rs 203 cr support cascade growth (S2, S3). Hydrogen remains optionality, with no revenue yet.

companies.name: Confidence Petroleum India Ltd
companies.role: LPG/CNG cylinder maker and distributor. Its step-down subsidiary Silversky Exim is setting up a Type 4 cylinder plant at MIDC Butibori, Nagpur (S15, S17).
companies.impact: No commissioning, certification or Type 4 revenue disclosed as of June 2026 (S15). Earnings are driven by LPG (S13). A modified FY26 audit opinion and Rs 761 cr of debt weigh on quality (S13, S16).

companies.name: Everest Kanto Cylinder Ltd
companies.role: Seamless steel high-pressure cylinder maker. USD 5.5 mn capex approved at its US subsidiary for larger-diameter and Type 4 cylinders (S18).
companies.impact: Type 4 is a US-based, small-ticket expansion. Indian CNG steel-cylinder volumes are weak, with Q1 FY27 revenue down 10.5% and PAT down 41.5% (S19).

companies.name: Reliance Industries Ltd
companies.role: Building an advanced-materials facility for composites used in hydrogen storage, and a carbon-fibre plant at Hazira (S22). A Tracxn listing shows an entity named Reliance New Energy Carbon Fibre Cylinder Limited (S23). Also an NGHM pilot participant (S20).
companies.impact: Potential localiser of imported carbon fibre (S9). Immaterial to group earnings.

companies.name: Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd
companies.role: Buyer of Type IV composite LPG cylinders (HP Navya), supplied by Time Technoplast for the Swiggy Instamart pilot (S5). Also an NGHM hydrogen-vehicle pilot participant (S21).
companies.impact: Demand-side adopter. Composite cylinders support new LPG retail formats (S5).

companies.name: GAIL (India) Ltd
companies.role: Joint-venture parent of Maharashtra Natural Gas, which placed a Rs 134 cr Type IV CNG cascade order with Time Technoplast in 2023 (S7).
companies.impact: CGD-side buyer of cascades. Exposure is indirect and immaterial.

companies.name: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd
companies.role: Co-parent of MNGL (S7) and an NGHM hydrogen-vehicle pilot participant (S20, S21).
companies.impact: Demand-side for cascades and hydrogen storage. Immaterial to earnings.

companies.name: Indian Oil Corporation Ltd
companies.impact: Pilot hydrogen fleets need onboard Type III/IV storage. Volumes are pilot-scale (S20).

companies.name: KPIT Technologies Ltd
companies.role: Named among the 12 NGHM hydrogen-vehicle pilot participants (S20).
companies.impact: Indirect: a hydrogen mobility pilot participant, not a cylinder maker.

companies.name: Ashok Leyland Ltd
companies.role: Awarded an NGHM hydrogen bus/truck pilot in the March 2025 round (S21).
companies.impact: Potential OEM customer for onboard hydrogen cylinders once pilots scale. Currently pilot-scale (S21).

method: First edition, researched 23-24 Oct 2026 with web searches and page fetches. Sources are exchange filings (NSE/BSE), a government page (TDB), a Motilal Oswal results note (PDF read directly), market-research pages, Screener.in data as of the 23-Oct-2026 close, and news reports. FY26 composite revenue for Time Technoplast is the sum of MOFSL's quarterly segment figures (Rs mn converted to Rs cr). Several primary PDFs (TIME 250 L press release, EKC presentations, BSE filings) timed out or returned 403. Facts from them are cited from search-result summaries of those documents, and S23 is a search listing that was not opened. Claims that could not be confirmed were left out: Confidence's Rs 350 cr / 1-3 lakh unit figures, final PESO approval of the 250 L cylinder, and any notified hydrogen-CNG blending mandate. The brief's TDB-funded NTF plant is an unlisted company, not Time Technoplast. Broker ratings and price targets are deliberately excluded.

certified_manufacturers: Listed companies with approved Type IV products or firm orders in India
capacity_builders: Listed companies with publicly stated Type IV plants or capex but earlier-stage or unproven execution
